source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rate_sensitive.evidence: Emcure reduced outstanding debt in FY25 through scheduled repayments and working capital management; debt-to-equity improved to ~15.8%, but floating vs fixed-rate split is not disclosed in available sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedging by offsetting foreign currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign currency receivables; residual exposure managed via financial instruments/operational measures.
inr_exposure.evidence: Emcure IR/press commentary: company offsets FC payables against FC receivables as a natural hedge; international business (~54% of FY25 revenue, incl. Emerging Markets, Europe, Canada) implies material multi-currency exposure, though a specific USD% is not disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure is one of 9 companies approved in Group B of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals/APIs (KSMs, drug intermediates, APIs), aimed at reducing import dependence on China; company-specific revenue benefit not disclosed.

rural.evidence: Management commentary (Q3FY25 earnings call) notes rural and semi-urban markets growing ~1.5x faster than urban; distribution footprint expanded to 38,500 towns (from 18,000 in 2020), including 'Pidilite Ki Duniya' outlets targeting villages of 5,000-10,000 population. No exact rural revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM (vinyl acetate monomer), a petrochemical/crude-oil derivative, has been repeatedly cited across broker/press commentary as accounting for roughly 30-40% of Pidilite's raw material costs (e.g. 'VAM forms 35-40% of overall raw material costs'); VAM price volatility is a recurring margin driver in quarterly results commentary.

inr_exposure.evidence: Pidilite operates ~19 overseas subsidiaries (5 direct, 14 step-down) plus a JV across USA, Thailand, Dubai, Brazil, Egypt, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Kenya; international business reported at ~Rs 647 crore in FY25 (a small share of ~Rs 13,400 crore consolidated revenue), implying limited but non-zero USD/other FX exposure. Hedging policy not found in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India press/IR commentary: company exports to over 100 countries and has invested >$230M over the past decade (plus a further $75M announced) to strengthen India as a global manufacturing hub for electrification and automation products serving both local and export/global demand; no explicit 'China+1' framing found, but clear export-momentum + manufacturing-diversification narrative.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India IR commentary (Q4 CY2024/CY2025 results): company described as a beneficiary of government capex in mega infrastructure, renewables, metro/railway electrification, data centers and grid modernization, with India's capex cycle framed as a structural multi-year driver of order growth. No specific % of revenue tied to govt/infra capex disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: ABB India generates revenue of >$1.5bn (2025), described as <4% of ABB Group global total; exports to 100+ countries noted, but no specific USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosure found.

rural.evidence: Analyst/industry commentary notes consumption growth in Tier-2/3/4 cities and rural areas could outpace urban cities, presenting a growth opportunity for USL; no specific rural revenue % disclosed in company sources found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company-level hedging policy for USL itself not found; parent Diageo plc's group treasury policy targets ~80% coverage of transactional FX exposure for the current year, and hedges 80-100% of net investment in foreign operations for USD/EUR (50-100% for other currencies).
inr_exposure.evidence: USL's Shaw Wallace Overseas exports to 37+ countries (UK, US, Australia, Singapore among key markets); export revenue is a minor share of overall business, which is dominated by domestic IMFL sales. Diageo group hedging policy cited as contextual proxy, not USL-specific disclosure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch India press releases note export sales increased within the Powertrain Solutions division (part of the Mobility business) in FY24/FY25, but no diversification-from-China or China+1 framing was found in available sources.

rural.evidence: Mobility business sales growth attributed partly to the tractor segment within Powertrain Solutions, an indirect proxy for rural/agri-linked demand; no explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch Limited received approval on 15 March 2022 under India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components ('Component Champion Incentive Scheme') for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products; incentives of up to 18% on incremental sales are available, but Bosch-specific revenue/incentive amount is not disclosed in sources found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company press releases (Q1FY27/Q3FY26) note export order growth from Europe, North America and South Asia (grid integration, power quality, HVDC), but no explicit 'China+1' framing was found in the accessible commentary; FY24-25 AR itself could not be fetched directly (hitachienergy.com and BSE/NSE filing hosts were blocked in this environment).

govt_capex.evidence: Hitachi Energy India supplies grid infrastructure, substations and HVDC equipment; management commentary (Q4FY25/Q4FY26 press releases) attributes demand to India's grid build-out, renewable integration and data-centre driven power demand growth, but no revenue % linked specifically to government capex is disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Recent investor commentary (Q1FY27 results/slides) states export markets account for approximately 25% of both revenue run-rate and order backlog; precise FY24-25 AR figure could not be confirmed as the AR PDF was inaccessible.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme (Auto PLI, ACC battery PLI, etc.) applicable to power transmission/grid equipment manufacturing was identified for the company.

rural.evidence: MD & CEO's message, Integrated AR FY2024-25: 'the rural segment showed signs of recovery, supported by improved agricultural output and rising income levels... This resurgence offered a degree of stability to an otherwise subdued performance across the industry,' with rural/semi-urban markets cited as a medium-term growth driver.

govt_capex.evidence: Directors' Report/MD&A FY2024-25: 'the run-up to the General Election saw a temporary reduction in government infrastructure spending, further dampening demand' during the year; separately, 'Government's thrust on infrastructure development and the Make in India initiative has further fuelled demand' for the Industrial/Protective Coatings segment (Industrial paints revenue Rs 1,839.80 Cr, ~16% of standalone Decorative+Industrial revenue).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Financial Capital section, Integrated AR FY2024-25: 'We maintained zero gross debt with an improving net cash position, reflecting our strong fundamentals.' Debt/EBITDA ratio was 0.34x, and current borrowings were nominal, used only for working capital.

crude_exposure.evidence: Note 37, Consolidated Financials FY2024-25: Cost of materials consumed was Rs 5,874.69 Cr against revenue from operations of Rs 11,544.71 Cr (~50.9%). Paint raw materials (titanium dioxide, solvents, resins) are significantly crude-oil-derivative linked per industry commentary; MD&A also cites 'volatile raw material prices' as a margin factor.

inr_exposure.evidence: Note 35.1(B), Consolidated Financials FY2024-25: Revenue from operations outside India was Rs 847.33 Cr of Rs 11,457.48 Cr (~7.4%). Company is a net importer of forex (Foreign Exchange Outgo Rs 1,195.75 Cr vs Earnings Rs 3.17 Cr, standalone), so INR depreciation risk is primarily on the import/cost side; MD&A cites 'currency volatility' as a margin pressure factor.

pli_scheme.evidence: Paints/coatings sector is not covered under any major PLI scheme; no PLI participation is disclosed anywhere in the FY2024-25 Integrated Annual Report.

inr_exposure.evidence: Per DRHP/IPO-note commentary, exports contributed approximately 5.4% of manufacturing revenue in FY24 (~94.6% domestic), reflecting Belrise's predominantly India-focused 2-wheeler metal components business with export footprint in US, Japan, UK and China.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY24-25/FY25-26 commentary describes a supply-chain shock from China's export ban on rare-earth magnets disrupting production of key Royal Enfield models (Himalayan, Scram, Guerrilla) — this reflects a China-dependency risk rather than a China+1 diversification benefit narrative.

rural.evidence: Media/analyst commentary indicates Royal Enfield sees rural 2-wheeler demand as a growth driver, with 'rural demand rising and continuing to outpace urban sales growth' cited by company management, though not quantified as a revenue % in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield exports were ~100,136-107,143 units in FY2024-25 out of ~1.0-1.01 million total units sold (~10-12.5% of volume/turnover), across 65+ countries; hedging policy not disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors was approved as a 'Champion OEM' under the Auto PLI Scheme (Champion OEM Incentive Scheme for Advanced Automotive Technology products) per Ministry of Heavy Industries PLI Auto scheme approvals; incentive amount/revenue impact not disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analysis (moneymuscle.in FY25 review) states export orders from Europe and Asia 'grew amid a China+1 supply-chain shift' and that TDPS is 'well-placed to benefit from global supply chain shifts, as many OEMs prefer sourcing from non-Chinese suppliers'; this framing is from analyst commentary, not confirmed as verbatim language from the Annual Report itself (which was not directly accessible).

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses forward booking/hedges for currency management and benefits from a natural hedge as both copper imports and generator/alternator exports are largely denominated in USD/EUR, per Q4FY25 earnings-call commentary; hedges were noted to be 'rolling off' amid copper price increases, posing a margin risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export and deemed-export order inflow was approximately 68-70% of total orders in FY2024-25 per earnings-call and analyst commentary (product installed base spans 105-113 countries); precise revenue-basis export % not confirmed from the AR directly.

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/company commentary (BusinessToday, Jun 2026): Zydus is reducing Chinese API sourcing from ~46% toward a target of ~35%, and MD Sharvil Patel notes India's PLI schemes and tax incentives have enabled capacity expansion in formulations/APIs, positioning Zydus to capture China+1 supply-chain diversification demand.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Treasury reported to combine natural hedges (USD receivables vs payables) with forward contracts/options; exact hedge ratio not confirmed from primary AR text (third-party analysis, moderate confidence).
inr_exposure.evidence: US Formulations ~47% of consolidated revenue (Q3FY25 print); large USD-denominated receivables base makes INR/USD a material earnings driver.

pli_scheme.evidence: MD Sharvil Patel: Govt PLI schemes and tax incentives for pharma have enabled Zydus's capacity expansion across formulations and APIs; exact PLI revenue/incentive amount not disclosed in sources reached.

china_plus_one.evidence: Trade/industry commentary: global demand for Indian wires & cables from North America and Europe has surged, with Indian manufacturers holding UL/CPR/AS-NZS certifications capturing China+1 diversification demand from Western utilities/contractors qualifying alternative suppliers; not exclusively attributed to Finolex in company disclosures found, and exports remain a small (~2-3%) share of Finolex's own revenue.

rural.evidence: Agricultural-application cable volumes fell ~15-16% YoY in a recent quarter due to monsoon/pre-seasonal impact, indicating some rural/agri demand linkage, but no % of total revenue from rural markets was disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Management cites infrastructure spending, housing completions, and government electrification pushes (e.g. Northeast/Assam expansion) as demand drivers for the electrical cables segment; no specific revenue % quantified.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has historically been described as near debt-free with minimal interest expense, suggesting low floating-rate liability exposure; no specific % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs are copper/aluminium conductors and PVC compound insulation (PVC is a crude-oil derivative); exact % of raw material cost attributable to PVC/crude-linked inputs was not found in sources reached.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue is a small share of total (management targeting 2-3% over two years, up from ~30cr to ~52cr); rupee depreciation has been cited as a margin pressure via costlier copper/raw material imports.

Q4FY25/FY25 geography split (investor presentation, via search): Americas ~46.1%, EMEA ~21.2%, Rest of World ~13.2% of revenue; remainder likely UK/APAC reporting nuance not fully reconciled from sources reached. As an Indian IT exporter, India/domestic revenue is understood to be a low single-digit % of total, though an exact disclosed figure could not be confirmed.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY25 results coverage: European subsidiaries secured new order wins (incl. ~EUR40mn from VW and BMW in EV/hybrid segments) and the group expanded internationally via acquisitions (e.g. 60% stake in Stoferle, Germany, ~EUR80mn revenue), reflecting export/diversification momentum; no explicit 'China+1' framing was found directly attributed to Endurance in sources reached.

crude_exposure.evidence: Product mix includes plastic/rubber components alongside aluminium die-casting, suspension and braking parts; plastics/rubber are crude-oil derivatives, but exact % of raw material cost from crude-linked inputs was not found in sources reached.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~23.6% of FY25 consolidated revenue came from European operations (EUR-denominated: full-year Europe turnover ~EUR391.7mn), exposing the group to EUR/INR movements; specific hedging policy not found in sources reached.

pli_scheme.evidence: Endurance is a Tier-1 auto-components supplier of a type eligible for the PLI-Auto (Component Champion) scheme (Rs 25,938 cr outlay, ~75-85 approved beneficiaries including Tata Autocomp, Motherson, Bosch, Lucas-TVS), but explicit confirmation of Endurance's own approval/participation could not be found in sources reached.

rural.evidence: Company is actively expanding into underpenetrated Tier-3/Tier-4 towns and smaller Tier-2/3 cities in north/east India (18 new labs added in FY25, plus new labs in Bengaluru/Hyderabad/Pune/Goa) as a stated growth strategy; no specific % of revenue from rural/Tier-3+ markets was disclosed in sources reached.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported to carry low leverage (debt-to-equity ~7.1%, debt well covered by operating cash flow), limiting floating-rate liability exposure; no specific floating-rate % disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: MD&A/analyst summaries of Divi's FY24-25 AR materials: 'multi-national innovator companies are actively moving to diversify their supply chains... shift volume to highly compliant, large-scale Indian contract manufacturing players to de-risk'; company cites 'China plus one opportunities' and a ~$20bn addressable opportunity from molecules going off-patent, positioning itself as a beneficiary via long-term supply agreements with global pharma.

crude_exposure.evidence: Analyst/press summaries note solvent costs (crude/petrochemical-derived) 'doubled or tripled' amid Middle East geopolitical tensions, a key input cost driver; imports account for ~45% of raw material consumption, cited as a natural hedge. No explicit crude-oil % of COGS disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge via ~45% imported raw materials; fixed exchange-rate contracts with major clients sharing FX fluctuation risk; selective hedging transactions entered as needed rather than a blanket policy.
inr_exposure.evidence: 87% of FY24 revenue from exports (largely USD-denominated); company reported a net forex loss of INR7cr in a subsequent quarter vs a gain of INR39cr prior year, showing residual unhedged exposure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Press coverage (Business Standard, mid-2025) reports Uno Minda 'eyeing local magnet production amid China disruptions'/curbs on rare-earth exports, exploring domestic manufacturing of rare-earth magnets to reduce China dependency. This is an import-substitution/de-risking narrative rather than an explicit export-order-growth China+1 framing, so classified moderate rather than strong.

rural.evidence: Two-wheeler segment (~35-40% of revenue) commentary links growth to 'resilient rural mobility demand' and expected improvement in rural incomes post-monsoon, but no explicit rural revenue % is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has outstanding fixed-coupon NCDs (7.11%/7.12%), suggesting a meaningful portion of debt is fixed-rate; consolidated debt-to-equity ~40%. No explicit floating-rate liability % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: India accounts for ~89% of revenue vs ~11% international in recent quarters; management has separately cited a target to raise 'international revenue' toward 40% by 2026 from ~26%, a figure that may use a broader consolidated-subsidiary definition — the two figures are not fully reconciled in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Business Standard (Dec 2025): Uno Minda named among five auto-component makers (with Varroc Engineering, Dana TM4 India, Napino Auto & Electronics, Cummins Technologies India) set to start receiving incentives under the Auto PLI scheme from FY27.

china_plus_one.evidence: Netweb's growth narrative is domestic import-substitution rather than export-side China+1: it benefits from India's 'Make in India' push, the IndiaAI Mission (~Rs 10,300cr allocation FY25-29 for domestic compute infra) and National Supercomputing Mission 2.0 favoring indigenous OEMs over imported (often China-sourced) servers. Export revenue is only ~5-9% of sales, so no material export business exists to support an export-oriented China+1 classification.

govt_capex.evidence: Multiple analyst/earnings-call summaries state '~50% of FY25 revenue came from government-linked customers,' reflecting Netweb's exposure to government data-center, HPC and AI-infrastructure procurement.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue cited at roughly 5-7% of total revenue (9.0% in one quarter), with the vast majority of sales domestic/INR-denominated.

pli_scheme.evidence: Business Standard/EquityBulls (Apr 2025): Netweb received a PLI Scheme 2.0 (IT Hardware) incentive of Rs 5.93 crore for the period 1 July 2023 - 31 March 2024.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/industry summaries of Navin Fluorine's positioning: the company 'stands to gain from supply chain diversification' and has 'started receiving new enquiries from companies looking to diversify supply chains out of China'; it has also backward-integrated via a 25% JV in India's only fluorspar beneficiation company plus long-term contracts with South African miners specifically to reduce China-sourcing dependency for a key mineral input.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution reported at 56% of FY25 revenue (down from 65% in FY24), with quarterly export mix ranging 43%-77% across FY25, driven by Specialty Chemicals/CDMO order timing.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is asset-light with minimal debt (debt-to-equity ~2.4%, down from ~16.9% five years ago; EBIT/interest coverage ~30x), suggesting negligible interest-rate sensitivity, though no floating-vs-fixed borrowing split is disclosed.
